doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Other Cuban drummers and friendly competition
summary: Tata Guines and others he knew personally but never played with; drummers recommended each other for jobs and rivalry was never hateful.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Maestro you told me of Chano Pozo, you told me about Mongo, you told me about you. What other drummers of that era were involved, that today are recognized on that level that you remember?
For example let's see, Tata Guines and now among those that are new, Los Papines, Los Muñequitos de Matanzas, there are many.
And you eventually played with each of them?

Well, musically no. Personally, yes. Like friends, "Oh how are you?" and this and that but musically no. I know them from the time period. And they also know me, but we never shared musically, only personally as friends, talking about music and the neighborhood and stuff. Quite interesting.
You never competed with them professionally?
Musically, say to get a gig with an orchestra.
No no no on the contrary, it was quite the opposite.

Exactly, exactly and when you could not do a job, you recommended your friend and the friend went. No matter how good he was, even if he was inferior or whatever but the friend was recommended. There was none of that. There was competition to excel, but not hatred and that is very important. Yes.
